summary: Genesis Project's one-screen C64 demo, third in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2012: a cluttered beach scene by Redcrab where a man plays a heap of instruments, with dogs and gadgets bopping along to the tune.
why: Sceners call it a charming, funny feel-good demo with something always happening on screen. They single out the detail in Redcrab's graphics and his funky tune, with animations triggered by the SID data.

quote.text: I love how the trumped oscillates with the vibrato, it's little details like that that made this demo so cool.

summary: Samar's C64 tribute demo to group founder Mariusz (Ramos), placed 2nd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Riverwash 2015, built around a huge scrolling painted image with background pictures.
why: Sceners call it a moving, honest tribute, singling out Isildur's artwork, the scrolling tile and background images, and the emotional soundtrack by Jammer and Pece.

quote.text: Very neat tribute demo. Full of sadness. Everything fits together.

summary: A short C64 intro by Tristar and Red Sector Inc., placed 2nd in the Oldschool Realtime Demo compo at Nordlicht 2013: an animated four-colour forest logo by CONS over a big text font, with code and charset by Streettuff and music by Linus.
why: Sceners single out the cute animated graphics, especially the Commodore balloon and the rabbit, along with the charset, the dramatic opening and Linus's experimental tune. Short, but conceptually entertaining.

quote.text: Nice, I really dig the dramaturgic opening, animation, charset, and the balloon of course. ;)

summary: Target Team's ZX Spectrum invitation for the Hackers Top 2010 Spring Edition party, with code by Restorer, graphics by Breeze and music by MmcM.
why: A party invitation from the Spectrum scene, made by a three-person crew and well received on Pouët.
highlights: dithered twister beside a scrolling text bar

summary: Radiance's Atari 8-bit demo for a 1MB-expanded machine, which won the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k24 WE. Code by Dante, music by Jammer, graphics by Blasph and Biter.
why: A first place at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, and it made the Meteoriks 2025 watchlist.

summary: A BBC Micro demo by CRTC, coded by Puppeh and Joey with music by Insectecutor, that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Sundown 2010.
why: It took first place in the Oldschool Demo competition at Sundown 2010, a win for the BBC Micro against other old machines.

summary: Arise's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at North Party 2006, coded by Fenek with graphics by Bimber and music from Jammer, Randall and Rodney, done almost entirely in colourful hires.
why: Sceners praised its fresh hires style, fast realtime vectors and morphs, and a sync with the music that holds it together. Later viewers called it years ahead of the hires revival demos that followed.

quote.text: The amout of real realtime coding without any precalc or animation trickery in this one is breathtaking.

summary: Hooy-Program's 2011 ZX Spectrum intro starring Nyan Cat, with code and music by Gasman and text and font by Aki.
why: A Spectrum take on the 2011 Nyan Cat meme, made the same year the meme took off. It's a light, cheerful piece from Hooy-Program with a scrolling message and a soundtrack by Gasman.

summary: Metalvotze's Vectrex demo, coded by Nitro, which won both the Alternative Demo/Intro compo and the Jury prize at Buenzli 2005.
why: A rare demo for the vector-display Vectrex that took two first places at Buenzli 2005, winning its compo and the jury's vote.

summary: A VIC-20 demo by Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, with code, graphics and music by Viznut and fullscreen pictures by ccr. It placed 2nd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2001.
why: A rare VIC-20 entry that held its own against other old machines in a major party's oldskool compo, taking second place at Assembly 2001.

summary: Quadtrip's C64 demo that came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2017, built around a glitch and noise theme, with code by visy and graphics by visy, Isildur and ZanaGB.
why: Sceners single it out as a model of how to use glitch aesthetics in a demo, praising the odd, twisted vibe and the unusual soundtrack by Jammer and Psycho8580.

quote.text: imho, this is the proper way to use glitch/noise theme in a demo. i enjoyed from beginning to end.

summary: An Atari VCS invitation for the SillyVenture 2012 party, released under Mystic Bytes with code by Tjoppen and music by Jakub Husak.
why: A rare demo-style invitation for the Atari 2600, made to announce the December 2012 SillyVenture party.

summary: Booze Design's single-file C64 demo, third in the Oldschool Demo compo at Edison 2018: a Jailbird logo screen with vector shapes passing through an animated ring, plus a scroller.
why: Sceners call it a polished, stylish one-screener, praising Jailbird's graphics, the fade-in, the vectors and the helix, and the detail of animating the ring.

quote.text: Love this! Really nice work. Lovely fade in, awesome vectors - and the helix.

summary: Arise's C64 demo, the third in their Biba series, placed 8th in the demo compo at X 2012. It mixes hi-res graphics, vector parts and bobs with a soundtrack by Randall, Rodney and Wacek.
why: Many sceners felt it was underrated at X 2012. They praise its coherent, original style, its hi-res graphics and its soundtrack, and some say they return to it regularly.

quote.text: I see myself boot this one up quite regularly, really really like it a lot and it doesnt grow old. coherent design, superb soundtrack, excellent code, originality, flow, its got it all.

summary: Tochi is a 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by Busy and Noro, with Busy credited for graphics and Noro for music. It came second in the ZX Spectrum 1K Intro compo at Forever 2017.
why: A second place in a dedicated 1K compo at Forever, from two long-standing Spectrum sceners, packing visuals and music into a kilobyte.

summary: A Sharp MZ-700 demo by Flush and Up Rough, with code and graphics by MooZ and p0ke, extra graphics by AdorU and music by Glafouk. It won the Oldskool Demo compo at Cookie 2017.
why: A compo-winning demo for a rarely seen machine, the Sharp MZ-700. It comes from a joint effort by two groups.

summary: Noice's C64 comeback demo, placed 6th in the C64 Demo compo at Datastorm 2014. Goat-themed parts with raytraced goats, a mirrored techtech and a multicolour end-scroller over a bitmap animation, with music by Dane.
why: Sceners welcomed it as a cheerful return for Noice, singling out the raytraced and rotating goats, the mirrored techtech, Dane's tune "Dear Brandon" and the progress bar, along with the name.

quote.text: Nice little demo, the mirrored techtech is my fave effect! The multicolored end-scroller with bitmap anim is also really nice..

summary: A 32K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Pulpo Corrosivo, with code by Toms, graphics by Beb and music by e-dredon. It won the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #4 in 2024.
why: It took first place in its compo at Benediction Coding Party #4. The video is labelled as showing the "wrong CRTC part", so this recording shows the intro on a particular CRTC variant.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo written in BASIC by Nodeus, who did code and graphics, with AY music by Moran. It came 2nd in the ZX-Basic compo at Base-X 2015.
why: Worth a look as a BASIC-only Spectrum demo that placed in a dedicated BASIC compo, showing what can be done without machine code on a 48K machine with AY sound.

summary: SquoQuo's Atari 8-bit invitation to Revision, released at Datastorm 2013 where it placed 2nd in the Other Platform Demo compo. Code by Hopper, graphics by Hopper, Raven and Farfar, music by 505.
why: An Atari 8-bit invite for one of the big demoparties, good enough to take second place against other platforms at Datastorm 2013.

summary: Bitshifters' BBC Micro demo that plays the Bad Apple video in teletext graphics, with intro artwork by Horsenburger and music by Inverse Phase.
why: A teletext take on the Bad Apple video. The silhouette animation is drawn in chunky Mode 7 block graphics, and the source is available.

summary: Defence Force's Oric demo for Kindergarden's 20th birthday, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Kindergarden 2014. Code by Dbug, graphics by Fra and Dbug, music by Count Zero.
why: A compo winner that takes its cue from Amiga cracktros, done on the Oric. Its video title calls it an "amiga cracktro" inspired intro made to mark the party's 20th birthday.

summary: Fatzone's C64 demo that won the Other Platform Demo compo at Gerp 2022, with code by Malmix and Pezac, graphics by Malmix and music by mAZE and Klegg.
why: Sceners praise its flow, smooth transitions and fresh twists on familiar effects. They single out the selfie squasher, a guitar-shredding animation and the colourful detail throughout.

quote.text: An entertaining feel-good code pr0n demo with very clever ideas, and in your own style.

summary: Samar Productions' C64 demo, released as an 80% party version, that won the C64 demo compo at Moonshine Dragons 2022. Code by Golara, Mojzesh and Slajerek, graphics by Isildur and Jetan, music by MCH, Conrad and Jammer.
why: Sceners praise its pace and flow, its 90s-style maths effects and the pixel work by Jetan and Isildur. The dotted mushroom intro and the Flip It part come up again and again.

quote.text: Ultra-stylish, precisely what I want from a Samar production. The flow of the parts is breathless; I can't see how anyone could get bored watching it.

summary: A 16K Atari 8-bit intro by g0blinish, with music by Dhor, that won the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k17.
why: It took first place in its compo at Silly Venture 2k17, a solid showing for a one-coder 16K production on the Atari XL/XE.

summary: Light's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at The Party 1991, with code by Flamingo, Waco, Rash and Yabba, graphics by Goblin and Scooby, and music from Bappalander, Bluez, Page and guest Danko.
why: Sceners who were at The Party 1991 remember it shaking the compo, and HCL calls it probably the best Light demo. Comments single out the vectors, a raytracer for its era and Bappalander's tunes.

quote.text: Man, this demo really shook the compo. Even the amigapeople were dropping jaws in awe

summary: A 128-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Gasman of Hooy-Program that won the 128 Byte Intro compo at Outline 2018: a distorted blue and magenta chessboard pattern.
why: A compo winner at Outline 2018, and a 128-byte intro that fits sound in alongside its visuals.

summary: Taquart's Atari 8-bit demo, coded by Eru and Fox, which won the Atari 8bit Demo compo at Intel Outside 1997.
why: A compo winner from the late-1990s Polish Atari scene, and one of the better-regarded Atari 8-bit demos of its year.

summary: Chorus's one-file C64 demo that won the demo compo at Árok 2008, with code by Clarence, music by DRAX and Fanta, and graphics by Leon.
why: A coder's demo that sceners single out for its full-screen ECI tech-tech running at 50 fps, the diagonal Kefrens bars and the oldskool DYSP and FPD finale, plus Drax's music.

quote.text: ECI techtech looks quite impressive, I mean it is a colorful effect that covers almost entire C64 screen and runs 50 fps.

summary: Csabo's Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo that won the Pimp My Part compo at Busodore 2011, a contest where sceners rework a given part.
why: It took first place in its compo, and the source is available for anyone curious about how it was done on the Plus 4.

summary: Hoaxers and Wrath Designs' underwater-themed C64 demo, winner of the demo compo at Transmission64 2021 Fall Edition, with code by Firehawk, graphics by Joe and music by Møllpauk.
why: Sceners praise Joe's graphics, the moody soundtrack and Firehawk's code, singling out the merging-outline scroller, side-border image movers and a coral scroller some had never seen before, all on a stock machine.

quote.text: Great graphics and moody soundtrack for submersive atmosphere, with outstanding coding that warrants a peek or two in the memory monitor.

summary: The Obsessed Maniacs' parody C64 demo, coded and scored by kb with a logo by Half-Elf, which placed 6th in the C64 demo compo at The Party 1994. It's a fake demo that sends up demo conventions.
why: Sceners call it the best fake demo on the C64 because it's well made rather than a lazy BASIC joke. They single out the dramatic music timed to the gags and the world's smallest scroller.

quote.text: People were suprised at every new effect, and laughed kind a' all the time.

summary: Offence's Space Invaders tribute for the C64, made entirely by Kristian Myklebust and winner of the Oldskool Demo compo at Kindergarden 2013. Invaders are rebuilt from isometric cubes, alongside a convincing recreation of the arcade screen.
why: Sceners praise its timing and design, its minimal music synced to the action, and the way the font is reworked to look like the original arcade machine. A one-man effort covering code, graphics and music.

quote.text: I love the concept, I love the execution, as usual your sense of timing, design and a strange ability to make minimalistic music sound super cool is present.

summary: A 128-byte intro for the Atari 2600 VCS by Tjoppen, which placed second in the 128 Byte Intro compo at Outline 2012.
why: A 128-byte VCS intro that includes sound and took second place at Outline 2012. The source code is available for anyone curious how it fits.

summary: Ilmenit's 256-byte intro for the Atari XL/XE, placed second in the Oldschool Intro 256b compo at Demodulation 2020: a snowy night road running towards a striped rising moon.
why: It won Best Oldschool Tiny Intro at The Nano Awards 2021, so it is one of the most recognised 256-byte Atari productions of its year.

summary: Genesis Project's C64 invitation to Datastorm 2014, coded and drawn by Mermaid with music by Stinsen: a cartoon car drives along beneath a big Datastorm logo while coloured bubbles drift and the party details scroll past.
why: Sceners call it cosy and singled out Stinsen's tune, the smooth animation of the car and the custom Frankfurter-style charset Mermaid drew for it.

quote.text: Really good idea and perfect animation of the sweet car and the colors flying around!

summary: Atari Inc.'s 1980 in-store demonstration program for the Atari 8-bit computers, coded by Mike Albaugh: a sales loop of captioned screens pitching the machine for home entertainment and family education.
why: A commercial demo from the very start of the Atari 8-bit line, made to sell the machine in shops. It's an early piece of the platform's history rather than a scene production.

summary: Ate Bit's ZX Spectrum demo, coded and drawn by evilpaul with music by Gasman, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2006.
why: A podium finish at Sundown 2006 for a small two-person Spectrum team, with evilpaul handling both code and graphics.

summary: Ate Bit's 1K invitation intro for Sundown 2007 on the ZX Spectrum, released at Breakpoint 2007, where it placed 7th in the Console/Real Wild compo.
why: A party invitation squeezed into one kilobyte on the Spectrum, with a solid reception on Pouët.

summary: Game Boy demo by Matt Current, with code and graphics by Janne and music by Sauli, shared 5th in the demo compo at Stream 2006. The video shows it running on a real DMG-001.
why: A placing at Stream 2006 and a solid reception on Pouët make it a good look at what the original Game Boy could do in 2006. It uses the Carillon player for its music and runs as an endless loop.

summary: Arsenic's C64 demo from Little Computer People 2011, where it placed 5th in the C64 demo compo. Code by Axis and Peiselulli, music by Fanta, graphics from Celtic, Sphinx, Veto and Yazoo.
why: Sceners single out the chainsaw-wielding ninja carving the logo into rock, the colourful vertical bending bars, the Mandelbrot part and Fanta's soundtrack. Several called it their favourite of the party despite its placing.

quote.text: It has the right mixture between creative ideas, technical brilliance and beauty. I also love the transitions.

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Gasman, who did the code, music, graphics and text himself. It placed 7th in the Wild demo compo at Assembly 2002.
why: A one-person piece of scene poetry that tells its story through on-screen text. It also uses the Spectrum's multicolour mode, beating the machine's usual colour limits.

summary: Blowjobb's monochrome Atari 8-bit demo, coded by Śmigło with graphics by dely and music by Miker. It placed third in the demo compo at Glucholazy 2008.
why: A third place at Glucholazy 2008, and a tidy example of an Atari demo working entirely in monochrome.

summary: Cluster's 4K intro for the Atari 2600, coded and directed by Kylearan with music by Glafouk. It placed third in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2017.
why: A podium finish at Revision for a 4K intro on one of the most constrained machines around, from a group that works on the VCS.

summary: Speccy.pl's ZX Spectrum 128K slideshow demo, with graphics by Piesiu, music by CatMan and code by Tygrys. It won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at speccy.pl party 2022.1.
why: A compo winner built around Piesiu's artwork. The video title calls it a slide show, so the pictures are the main draw, with CatMan's music behind them.
highlights: bearded man with headphones and pipe

summary: Flush's Atari 2600 demo M, coded by flewww with graphics and music by Glafouk, placed 2nd in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k18.
why: A second place in the dedicated VCS demo compo at Silly Venture 2018, from a small team getting big chunky graphics out of the 2600.

summary: A single-part Commodore 64 demo by kompositkrut: a SID cover of the Amazing Horse tune played over a scrolling parallax landscape with a sprite rider on a horse and a colour-cycling logo.
why: Sceners mostly praise the catchy SID cover, with the cheerful presentation of sprites, parallax scenery and fades as a fun extra. Originally released as a music piece and later listed as a one-file demo.

quote.text: Sounds awesome in SID. Very catchy, it keeps spinning round in my head.

summary: A 128-byte intro for the Atari XL/XE by Marquee Design, coded by superogue, that won the Oldschool 128 Byte Intro compo at Lovebyte 2022.
why: A compo winner at Lovebyte 2022 in the 128-byte class, and a "making of" writeup is available on the Marquee Design site for anyone curious how it fits.

summary: Dentifrice's Atari VCS demo themed around Bomberman, which won the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k25 WE. Code by Kezax, music by Glafouk, graphics by Exocet.
why: A compo winner at Silly Venture on the 2600, and its source is available for anyone curious how it was done on such limited hardware.

summary: A VIC-20 demo by CNCD that placed 3rd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2002.
why: A podium finish at Assembly's oldskool compo, which makes it a rare chance to see the unexpanded-or-not little VIC-20 taking on bigger machines at a major party.
